subject: Re: Prefetch/heartbeat billing — anchored prefix & pilot concession

Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com

Subject: Prefetching + heartbeat — how will this show up on our invoice?

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re evaluating a retrieval-heavy flow that does a small prefetch (1–2k tokens) to prime the responder and then keeps a 30s heartbeat to maintain a warm KV cache for repeated patient-summary lookups. Our finance team flagged two specific concerns:

- Will the prefetch tokens be billed in full for every request, or can they be amortized/credited if they’re reused?
- How does the heartbeat (periodic lightweight calls) interact with minimums and rounding? We’ve seen other vendors count the heartbeat as a full call and it inflates cost.

Attached is a 2-week sample of usage (pilot_usage_sample.csv) — the pattern shows many short lookups with occasional long contexts. Can you provide a deterministic example calculation (how you’d round/prorate) and any possible concession for a pilot?

We’re trying to make sure the economics pencil for a 3-month pilot before committing to dedicated capacity.

Best,
Sophie
Sophie Grant
Head of Platform Integrations
Acme Health

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Prefetching + heartbeat — how will this show up on our invoice?

Hi Sophie — thanks for the sample and the clear questions. I pulled together a short walkthrough and two practical pilot options. Attached: anchored_prefix_calc.xlsx with line-item math. Summary below.

Executive summary (short):
- Prefetch tokens: by default billed as executed tokens. However, for retrieval-prefetch patterns we recommend an "anchored-prefix" approach that avoids double-counting repeated prefix prefetches for the same user session within a short time window.
- Heartbeat calls: treated as normal API calls; we can offer a lightweight heartbeat SKU (KB-level priced) for pilots instead of full generation pricing.
- Pilot concession: two options — (A) 90-day minimum-waiver up to an agreed cap, or (B) Prefetch-credit line item (monthly credit equal to 5% of billed tokens for the pilot).

Deterministic example (using your sample pattern):
Context: typical lookup does 1,800 token prefetch, then a 600-token prompt; server replies 120 tokens.
Base billing (no concession):
- Prefetch: 1,800 tokens billed on call initiation
- Prompt: 600 tokens billed
- Response: 120 tokens billed
Total raw tokens: 2,520 tokens per call.
Rounding/minimums: our hosted plan rounds billed tokens to the nearest 50-token quantum and applies a 100-token per-call minimum for streaming calls. For this pattern that results in:
- Rounded tokens: 2,550 (2,520 rounded up to nearest 50)
- Apply per-call minimums: not triggered (total > 100)

Anchored-prefix approach (recommended for retrieval flows):
- When a prefetched prefix is identical for subsequent calls within the same session (configured anchor window = 120s), we bill the prefetch once and mark subsequent calls as "prefix re-use". Example: two calls within 90s using same 1,800-token prefix => first call billed 2,550 (rounded), second call billed for prompt+response only (720 rounded to 750).
- This prevents the prefetch from being charged repeatedly when it’s effectively cached.

Prefetch credit option (pilot-friendly):
- Instead of waiving rates entirely, we can add a monthly credit line: 5% of token charges back to you during pilot months, up to $X cap. This preserves normal metering while smoothing invoice volatility.

Implementation notes (engineering):
Karthik — we’ll need a short metric to detect identical prefix hashes and a session anchor TTL (we typically use 120s). We can expose a header in responses when prefix re-use applies so customers can audit.

Next steps:
- Sophie — which pilot concession do you prefer (A: 90-day minimum-waiver; B: 5% prefetch credit)?
- I’ll coordinate with billing to include the credit line and with infra to expose the prefix-use header.
- If agreeable, we can schedule a 30-minute call to finalize cap numbers and the SLA for heartbeat SKU.

Regards,

Naomi — quick technical confirmation / alternate suggestion.

We can detect identical prefix prefetches with a cheap 64-bit hash and the session-id + ttl (120s) as you suggested. When we detect reuse we should:
- Emit X-Redwood-Prefix-Reuse: true in the response header.
- Bill the first call at normal rates (rounded quantum).
- For subsequent calls within anchor window, bill only prompt+response and a fixed 20-token bookkeeping charge (rounded to quantum) to cover metadata & cache maintenance.

On the pilot concession: instead of a hard 90-day waiver I prefer the prefetch-credit (5%) because it’s auditable and avoids a sudden post-pilot invoice cliff. We should also add an abuse guard:
- If identical prefix reuse rate < 10% and heartbeat volume is > 10k calls/day, escalate to billing ops for review.

Grace — can you confirm the cap range we’ll propose to Acme (I recall $5k–$15k monthly ranges for similar pilots)?

—Karthik
